PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, Sprint 43, commit a704928 on devteam2/sprint-43 (worktree). Verdict: PASS.

Sprint file: re-read fresh in the worktree. The only change since main's copy is the lifecycle status line (7794a72). It includes the struck-through portrait prerequisite (done, 24 Nov).

Handoff: read at a704928 with git show. It has a Round 1 section quoting VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0 with 39 files and 483 tests. QA1's own npm run verify in the worktree: verify=0, 39 files, 483 tests, VERIFY PASS. The screenshots and probe.json are committed under docs/handoffs/sprint-43/.

R1: met for the repository.
- docs/design/banner_variations.html has sha256 0dd05937...0ee3, the same as the primary checkout's untracked new_banner.html (QA1 hashed both).
- grep of app/ finds no banner_variations or new_banner.
- git ls-files new_banner.html in the primary checkout is empty; it was never tracked.
- The root copy still exists untracked in the primary checkout. The handoff says the user chose to delete it themselves. This is a Human Prerequisite (below), not a code defect.

R2: met. SiteBanner is one component (app/components/SiteBanner.tsx), mounted once in ReadingView as the card's first child, above the date band, and in the error boundary. Render paths QA1 confirmed:
- /date/[date] renders every state (write form, saved horoscope, unavailable, disabled, Sprint 39 unmatched or failed) through ReadingView.
- /reading/[id] renders written, unwritten, disabled and Sprint 39 states through ReadingView.
- /reading/[id] error.tsx mounts SiteBanner tagline null at the top of its card.
- notFound 404s are out of scope.
banner-pages.test.ts covers each through the real pages.

R3: met. There are two anchors to /. The wordmark is the one tab stop, with aria-label "Ask Reloy — home". The portrait anchor has tabIndex -1 and aria-hidden true. This is the sprint's named second option. Answer to Dev Team's question: acceptable, because the outcome R3 asks for is one tab stop and one announced link, and a tabindex -1 element inside aria-hidden is the accepted pattern (it doesn't trip the aria-hidden-focus rule). probe.json and the tests show one focusable / link at both widths, on both routes.

R4: met.
- public/reloy-seer.png sha256 63faa419...57db, 4255 bytes. QA1 decoded manifest entry a22c751d (mime image/png, not compressed) from the committed design file and got the identical hash.
- 133x138 CSS px, image-rendering pixelated; next/image is unoptimized (no resizing); no fractional px.
- Alt approach stated: alt is empty inside the aria-hidden duplicate link; the name is carried by the wordmark link.

R5: met. QA1 extracted the bundler template and compared it with 0a's header. Padding 16px 40px 0, the gradient, the 1px bottom border, align-items flex-end, the 24px portrait gap, the text column (gap 8px, padding-bottom 18px) and the wordmark (52px, weight 300, line-height 0.95, letter-spacing 0.005em, colour 0.94 0.012 85) all match. "Reloy" is italic, verdigris. The tagline matches the BYLINES style string in the script: 17px, italic, line-height 1.35, colour 0.74 0.02 85. Tokens are used where one has the exact value: --om-rule-strong and --om-verdigris are equal to the design's literals (checked in globals.css). The four remaining literals have no token with that value (grep of globals.css finds none). Fonts use var(--font-cormorant).

R6: met against 0e's first (Seer) header: padding 10px 18px 0, gap 12px, a 133x92 window with overflow hidden and margin-left -24px, the image margin-top -46px, the wordmark 32px with line-height 1 and padding-bottom 18px kept through .text, no menu button, and the tagline display none. The banner is static, so not sticky. The card at 900px or less is a height-auto flex column (Sprint 38), so the banner can't be squeezed. probe.json shows scrollWidth equal to innerWidth at 390.

R7: met. TAGLINES matches the sprint list verbatim, including the U+2019 apostrophes in number 16. It's a constant in code, and the test types the list out again.

R8: met.
- pickTagline(random) takes its source as a parameter, and both pages call it with Math.random after await connection().
- QA1 grepped every "use client" file in app and lib for Math.random, getRandomValues and randomUUID: none.
- The server HTML carries the tagline: the page tests render it, and probe.json's 10 curls gave 7 distinct taglines.

R9: met. There is no aria-live or role status. The tagline box has min-height, not height, and no overflow rule. The tagline-8 screenshot shows two lines, unclipped.

R10: met. layout.tsx is untouched, so metadata is unchanged. Below the banner, the diff is only the tagline prop and the mount, plus the error card's padding moved from .card to .cardBody with the same values. reading.module.css is untouched.
- Answer to Dev Team's question on connection() in /reading/[id]: no objection. It is required in spirit by R8 (a per-request pick must never be served from a prerender) and changes no output.

R11: met. The boundary tests (0 and just under 1, both edges of every slice), the list test (19 verbatim) and verify exit=0 as above.

R12: met; the handoff was read from the commit. Screenshots QA1 viewed: desktop-1440-banner against design-0a, phone-390-date-page against design-0e-seer, desktop-1440-tagline-8. They match the design apart from the removed nav and dots.

For Master Controller, not blocking: the error boundary shows the banner with no tagline. R2 requires the banner there and R8 forbids a client-side random pick, and error.tsx must be a client component, so the sprint file's requirements can't all hold literally in that state. The user resolved it in Dev Team 2's session ("banner, no tagline"). That decision currently lives only in the handoff and code comments. MC may want to record it (decisions log, or the sprint file at close; amending the sprint file now would require a fresh QA1 audit before dev-done).

Human Prerequisite: the user deletes the untracked new_banner.html from the primary checkout's root (/home/sam/workspace/workshop/my_little_raccoon). It's byte-identical to the committed design record, so nothing is lost. The R1 criterion "the root copy is gone" is only true once that's done.

Known limitations in the handoff (the phone portrait inset by the default 8px body margin; the 155px desktop cost) are disclosed and within R10's constraints. The screen-reader pass belongs to LiveQA's step 7.

Worktree return path: the branch is devteam2/sprint-43 and needs Pipeman's merge into main per CLAUDE.md. Main has moved since the branch point (Sprint 40's records); Pipeman merges. A merge that changes code content would need a re-audit before ship, per the tree-hash gate.
commit=4dd37e0 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 4dd37e0860944c77557d2311996adf1d043ab007 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). Steps 1 to 6 are done on production. Step 7 used Chromium's accessibility tree, because no screen reader could be run and observed from this session (what was tried is below). No defects.

Tested 2026-11-24, about 03:00 to 03:30 UTC, against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit 4dd37e0. Production serves the pushed tip dbaab21: /api/health/db reports status ok, connected true, commit dbaab21, with migrationVersion unchanged at 20261122152710_navigation_exact_date_readings. git diff --stat 4dd37e0 dbaab21 touches only sprint docs, registry.json, and the state files for Sprints 40 and 43.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) at 1440x1000 and at 390x844 (isMobile, hasTouch), with JS on and off; CDP touch drags and Accessibility.getFullAXTree; and curl.
The design was docs/design/banner_variations.html, opened over file:// in the same Chromium, where it unpacked itself (section 0a, and 0e's first header, the Seer).
R1 aside: new_banner.html is no longer in the primary checkout's root (ls: No such file or directory), so the Human Prerequisite is done.

STEP 1, desktop 1440 against 0a: PASS.
Computed styles, production and then 0a:
- header padding: 16px 40px 0 in both.
- The gradient and bottom border: 0a uses oklch literals, and production computes them as lab. All three colours, and the wordmark, "Reloy" and tagline colours, paint the same RGB on a canvas in both, for example 4,4,8 / 13,12,21 / 43,42,53 / 239,235,226 / 103,179,106 / 177,170,157.
- The wordmark is Cormorant Garamond, 52px, weight 300, line-height 49.4px and letter-spacing 0.26px in both. "Reloy" is italic in both.
- The tagline is 17px, italic, line-height 22.95px in both.
- The portrait: natural size 133x138, shown at 133x138, image-rendering pixelated.
Geometry: the portrait is at x 40..173 and the wordmark text starts at x 197 in both (0a's crop matches visually).
The PNG served at /reloy-seer.png is 200 image/png, 4255 bytes, with sha256 63faa419...57db, identical to public/reloy-seer.png.
There is no nav and no dots (0 nav, button or dot elements in the banner). Without the dots row, the tagline sits lower in the bar; the sprint allows that difference.
The banner is the card's first child, 1294 wide in a 1296 card, directly above the dateBand. document.title is still "Retroactive Horoscope".
Screenshots: s43-design-0a.png and s43-prod-banner-1440.png.

STEP 2, the tagline varies: PASS.
- 10 curls of /date/1969-07-20 gave 9 distinct taglines, read from the server HTML's header p.
- 40 browser reloads gave 16 distinct taglines (indices 2-11 and 14-19). All 16 match the sprint's list exactly, and 0 were outside it. That includes number 16 with U+2019 apostrophes ("Tomorrow’s wisdom for yesterday’s uncertainties.").
- The tagline was unchanged 6s after load. A MutationObserver saw 0 header mutations in the 8s after load, at both widths.
- Tagline 8 at 1440: clientHeight 46 and scrollHeight 46 (2 lines), overflow visible, not clipped. Screenshot: s43-tagline8-1440.png.

STEP 3, the home link: PASS.
- On a real click (desktop) and a real tap (390) of the portrait and of the wordmark, and on Enter on the focused wordmark: the client navigation fetched /?_rsc, then /date/2026-11-24. Sprint 41 hasn't shipped, so / still returns 307 to today's date. Every case ended on /date/2026-11-24 with the banner present and no errors.
- The banner holds 2 anchors to /. The portrait's has tabindex -1 and aria-hidden true. The wordmark's has aria-label "Ask Reloy — home".
- Tab order from a blurred page: first stop [BANNER] A "Ask Reloy — home" /, then the date INPUT. So the banner is exactly one tab stop.

STEP 4, phone 390x844 against 0e Seer: PASS.
- Padding is 10px 18px 0 in both, and the colours match.
- The portrait window is 133x92 with overflow hidden and margin-left -24px; the image margin-top is -46px; image-rendering is pixelated. These match 0e.
- The wordmark is 32px with line-height 32px in both.
- There's no tagline (display none) and no menu button.
- scrollWidth is 390.
- The banner scrolls with the page: position static. After a real touch drag on /date/1969-07-20, scrollY was 344 and the banner sat at -336..-233. On /reading/0b01c79f-..., scrollY was 194 and the banner sat at -186..-83.
- Screenshots: s43-design-0e.png and s43-prod-top-390.png.
Minor, not defects:
- The banner is 374 wide, inset by the default 8px body margin. Dev Team's handoff already discloses this.
- Phone letter-spacing computes 0.16px against 0e's normal. That's 0.005em carried over from desktop, and not visible at this size.

STEP 5, JavaScript off: PASS.
At 1440:
- The banner renders, with the tagline in the server HTML (for example "Revealing the inevitable, one occurrence at a time.", 2 lines, not clipped).
- The image loads (naturalWidth 133).
- Clicking the wordmark lands on /date/2026-11-24.
At 390: the banner and image render, the tagline is hidden as designed, and the wordmark link lands on /date/2026-11-24.
There were no console or page errors with JS on, so no hydration mismatch, on any page tested.

STEP 6, /reading/<id>, and the other states: PASS. On each page, the banner is the card's first child, above the dateBand, with a server-picked tagline:
- /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d (saved reading);
- /reading/9bd536d1-243f-49e7-8c59-af75b6d76067 (Sprint 39's unmatched state);
- /date/2026-12-16 (write form);
- /date/2031-05-09 (unmatched).
/date/1054-07-04 returns 404 with no banner, which is the notFound case the sprint puts out of scope.
The error boundary (a banner with no tagline) can't be triggered on production; QA1 and the page tests cover it.

STEP 7, screen reader: NO SCREEN READER RUN. I used the accessibility tree.
Tried:
- Orca: not installed (no orca binary). WSLg is present (/mnt/wslg, DISPLAY=:0), but installing Orca would need a system package change.
- NVDA: not installed under Program Files.
- Windows Narrator: present at /mnt/c/Windows/System32/Narrator.exe. I did not start it: it would speak on the user's own Windows desktop, and this session can neither hear nor read what it says.
Accessibility-tree evidence (Chromium's tree, which is what screen readers consume), via CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree from the header node:
- Desktop: the header (role sectionheader) contains link "Ask Reloy — home" (text "Ask ", "Reloy") and one paragraph with the tagline, for example "Let the heavens confirm your suspicions."
- Phone: the link alone; the hidden tagline is not exposed.
- The portrait link and image aren't exposed.
- There's no aria-live or role status in the banner.
- The page has one empty alert node outside the banner, with no DOM host a document query finds, consistent with Next.js's route announcer, which predates this sprint.
- There were 0 header mutations after load.
So the banner exposes one link plus one line of text, and announces nothing after load.
